A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VISTA study, with 30 readable pages including Appendices A-H. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching manuscript content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original benchmark evaluations, a human annotation study covering 140 conversations and 888 claims, ablations, and abstention and contradiction experiments (Sections 5-7 and appendices).

after.justification: v4.pdf retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, human annotations, ablations, and CoCoNot and RGM-Contradictions evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 7.2 and Appendix A retain the same claim decomposition, verification, categorization, memory updates, and optional turn-level contradiction judge.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AIS, BEGIN, FaithDial, FADE, CoCoNot, and RGM-Contradictions, with the same human-annotated subset. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: FActScore and LLM-as-Judge retain identical participation in the corresponding comparisons. The majority baseline in Table 3 and random baseline in Table 5 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4-7 and Appendix B retain the same model configurations, sample sizes, sampling rules, metrics, turn-label aggregation, ablation procedures, and inference-only evaluation settings.

E4.justification: The FaithDial ablations in Section 6.3, contradiction analysis in Section 7.2, annotation-disagreement analysis, confusion matrices, and abstention and contextual examples in Appendices D-H are identical.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 still specifies a single evaluation pass without averaging over seeds. McNemar testing in Appendix E and inter-annotator agreement reporting in Section 5 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including Tables 1-21 and Figure 2. DeepSeek VISTA's FaithDial accuracy remains 81.70% (Table 2), and CoCoNot abstention accuracy remains 90.6% (Section 7.1).

T1.justification: Definitions and mathematical content are identical. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are identical, retaining the same claims about sequential factuality assessment, benchmark performance, annotation reliability, and released annotations.

C2.justification: Interpretations of ablations, contradiction failures, and annotation discrepancies are unchanged. Section 9 and Appendix H retain the same limitations concerning context, model judgments, benchmark design, applicability, and inference cost.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C retain identical prompts, inference and quantization settings, software and computational-cost details, and annotation procedures. Code and data access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and citations throughout the manuscript match. VISTA's positioning relative to decomposition methods, LLM judges, and dialogue factuality benchmarks is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 5 January 2026 to v4 dated 14 March 2026, and PDF title metadata drops 'Score'. The printed title, manuscript wording, and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2, Tables 1-21, annotation-interface screenshots, captions, and placement are identical. Rendered pages show no layout changes beyond the version/date text update assessed under P1.

improvement.justification: The main text, appendices, figures, and tables retain the same scientific evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information. Updating the arXiv stamp and PDF title metadata produces no meaningful overall quality difference.
